newsitem.title: USA: FDA group recommends Nasalcrom sold OTC.
newsitem.headline: FDA group recommends Nasalcrom sold OTC.

text.p: Johnson & Johnson unit McNeil Consumer Products Co said on Thursday that a U.S Food and Drug Administration advisory committee recommended Nasalcrom to be switched from prescription to over-the-counter status.

Nasalcrom, which is used to prevent and treat symptoms of allergic rhinitis, was developed by Rhone-Poulenc Rorer subsidiary Fisons Corp and is licensed to McNeil Consumer for over-the-counter marketing in the United States.
If cleared by the FDA, Nasalcrom would be the first over-the-counter allergy treatment that was also used for prevention, McNeil said.

The company said that more than 40 million Americans suffered from allergic rhinitis. Nasalcrom 4 percent nasal solution was cleared by the FDA for marketing as a prescription drug in 1983. McNeil said the advisory committee was unanimous in recommending the status switch.
